nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order. For every $n$ segments in $\Bbbk^2$, each given by its two endpoints, ANY-SEGMENTS-INTERSECT costs at most $n^2 + 24n$, so it runs in time $O(n^2)$. Cost counts one unit per evaluation of DIRECTION or ON-SEGMENT.
nodes.title: Running time of ANY-SEGMENTS-INTERSECT

nodes.summary: For a segment $j$, write $l_j$ for its endpoint with the smaller $x$-coordinate, or for its first given endpoint when both $x$-coordinates agree, and $r_j$ for its other endpoint. For a point $q$, segment $j$ is below $q$ when $\mathrm{DIRECTION}(l_j, r_j, q) < 0$.
nodes.title: Segment strictly below a point

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order, let $p, q, r \in \Bbbk^2$, writing $p = (p_x, p_y)$ and likewise for $q$ and $r$, with $p_x < q_x$, and let $y_{pq}(x)$ be the height at $x$ of the line through $p$ and $q$. Then $\mathrm{DIRECTION}(p, q, r) = (q_x - p_x)\,(y_{pq}(r_x) - r_y)$.
nodes.title: DIRECTION as a scaled vertical offset

nodes.summary: For $n$ segments, the charge of an event is $n + 16$ if it is the left endpoint of a segment and $8$ if it is the right endpoint of a segment.
nodes.title: Cost charged to a sweep event

nodes.summary: For $n$ segments indexed by $0, \dots, n-1$, an event is a pair $(i, b)$ of a segment index $i$ and a Boolean $b$; it stands for the left endpoint of segment $i$ when $b$ is true and for its right endpoint when $b$ is false.
nodes.title: Sweep event

nodes.summary: For $n$ segments, each given by its two endpoints, the left endpoint of a segment is its endpoint with the smaller $x$-coordinate, or its first given endpoint when both $x$-coordinates agree, and the right endpoint is the other one. If $[p, q] \cap [p', q']$ is nonempty, then it contains a point $m$ with $m_1 \le w_1$ for every $w \in [p, q] \cap [p', q']$.

If running the sweep over $P$ from the empty status list succeeds with status list $T$, and running it over $Q$ from $T$ reports an intersection, then there are two distinct indices $i \ne j$ such that segments $i$ and $j$ meet.

nodes.title: Crossing of two non-vertical segments

nodes.summary: Let $f$ map a type to a linearly ordered set, let $y$ be a value, and let $T$ be a list sorted non-strictly by $f$, that is, $f(j) \le f(k)$ whenever $j$ occurs before $k$ in $T$. Suppose $b$ lies in $T$ with $f(b) = y$, and every element $c \ne b$ of $T$ has $f(c) \ne y$. Then removing from $T$ its longest prefix of elements $j$ with $f(j) < y$ leaves a list whose first element is $b$.
nodes.title: First element at or above a uniquely attained height

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered set and $S$ a family of segments in $K^2$, each given by its two endpoints. For every segment $i$ of $S$, the left endpoint event of $i$ is strictly smaller than its right endpoint event in the sweep order on events (by $x$-coordinate, then left endpoints before right endpoints, then by $y$-coordinate).
nodes.title: Left endpoint events precede right endpoint events

If the sorted sweep event list of $S$ is a list $P$ followed by a list $Q$, and $P$ contains the right endpoint event of a segment $j$, then $P$ also contains the left endpoint event of $j$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
